HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. KOREAN FACES on everyone in frame: living eyes with WHITE sclera, a catchlight, and BLACK ink-black iris and pupil (never brown, hazel, amber, blue, grey or green, never the whole eyeball painted solid black); a low soft Korean nasal bridge, never a high European nose. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. KOREAN WEBTOON movie still, dramatic manhwa COVER. NIGHT GROUND. Medium three-shot across a banquet table, low three-quarter. ONE device: Jamyeonggo as a vast dark circle behind the diners. LEFT of sheet = Choi Ri — FACE and red-cream court robe from /ch_choi_ri.png (goatee, dark headband, red po with cream dotted overlay, blue lower), tired father-king warning. SECOND = Hodong CLEAN-SHAVEN vermilion-russet. THIRD = Nakso dusty-gold. One table lamp. No crowd. Bold THICK ink. No text. No watermark. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = choiri, SECOND face = hodong, THIRD face = nakrangso. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), jougwan feather-cap board (shape only, ignore labels), binyeo board nakrangso (her hair ornament exactly; not clothing). KOREAN FACES on every person, named or extra: living eyes with WHITE sclera, a small catchlight, and BLACK ink-black iris and pupil (never brown, hazel, amber, honey, gold, blue, grey, green or purple). Never paint the entire eyeball solid black. A low soft Korean nasal bridge, never a high European, Roman or Persian nose. East Asian bone: single-lidded or low-creased eyes, straight or softly arched brows, broad cheekbones, flatter facial planes, warm ivory to sun-browned skin, straight coarse black hair. Never Western, Latin, or mixed-race features, never deep-set double-lidded western eyes. CHOI RI — Look: Mature Nakrang king: sharp almond eyes, faint knowing smile or grave line, well-groomed black goatee and moustache, dark hair in a topknot under a dark headband (not a jougwan). Dress: Commandery court silk from the portrait: wide-sleeved red outer robe, cream chest overlay with small red dots, dark cuffs, dark brown sash, blue lower garment. Night tragedy beats may mute the red but keep the silhouette. Colour #c45c4a. HODONG — Look: Young Goguryeo prince ~18–20: Jumong’s easy grin on a smaller face, clean-shaven, warm dark eyes, black hair half-bound under a small jougwan with twin pheasant feathers; open brow, boyish cheekbones. Dress: Goguryeo hunting silk — vermilion-russet (#d4563a) jeogori and po over dark trousers, rope sash, wrapped forearms; bow across the back when hunting. Court: red-brown layered robe, no crown. Colour #d4563a. NAKSO — Look: Young Nakrang princess ~17–19: soft oval Korean face, living black eyes that fill easily, long straight black hair half-loose with a simple gold pin (binyeo); flush-prone cheeks, bitten or parted lips when scared or wanting. Dress: Commandery-court silk: pale ivory jeogori and warm dusty-gold (#c9a06a) chima, soft sheen, few ornaments — not Silla gold dump, not Tang. Washing scenes: sleeves rolled, wet hems, undyed work cloth over the same face. Colour #c9a06a. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
